chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I heard Ali ibn Al-Husayn, the Ornament of the Worshippers (peace be upon them) say:

No step is more beloved to God, the Mighty and Majestic, than two steps: a step by which a believer reinforces a line in the way of God, and a step to a relative of kinship who has cut ties; and no sip is more beloved to God, the Mighty and Majestic, than two sips: a sip of wrath that a believer suppresses with forbearance, and a sip of calamity that a believer suppresses with patience; and no drop is more beloved to God, the Mighty and Majestic, than two drops: a drop of blood shed in the way of God, and a drop of tears shed in the darkness of the night by a servant who intends nothing by it except God, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.ذِي رَحِمٍ قَاطِعٍ: relative of kinship who has cut ties

ai.seo_question: What are the three pairs of actions most beloved to God according to Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these six 'beloved' acts to illustrate the balance between outward physical exertion (jihad, kinship ties) and inward spiritual discipline (forbearance, patience, night prayer). In Shia tradition, this hadith underscores the holistic nature of piety, where social connectivity and emotional regulation are elevated to the status of major acts of worship alongside physical sacrifice.
